source.title: Hedonic Neurons: A Mechanistic Mapping of Latent Coalitions in Transformer MLPs
source.authors: Tanya Chowdhury; Atharva Nijasure; Yair Zick; James Allan

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened or have disrupted column layout; aggregate results described in the prose are clearer than some individual table entries.
record.tranche_reason: Reports coalition and ablation results in LoRA-fine-tuned LLM rerankers, providing indirect evidence relevant to the LLM feature-distribution version. It does not test the toy-model superposition setup or its geometric predictions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures multi-neuron coalition synergy, coalition ablations, activation alignment, and coalition-based prediction in fine-tuned rerankers. These bear indirectly on V4. It does not test sparse overcomplete feature storage, capacity competition, SAE feature recovery or canonicality, or whether features are one-dimensional directions. The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and discusses SAEs, but those citations and discussion are not results. Layer selection values and comparisons among coalition-discovery algorithms are not separately included unless summarized as outcomes below.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces a game-theoretic method for finding neuron coalitions in LoRA-fine-tuned rerankers. Its results are that method's performance against clustering and random baselines: synergy, ablation drop, heuristic alignment and predictive R2. It never measures whether features are spread across more neurons than single units, or packed into fewer dimensions than features. It runs no SAE recovery, toy-model geometry or capacity test. It cites Toy Models and discusses SAEs and polysemanticity, but uses neither as a tool nor tests them. So no claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that hedonic coalitions beat clustering baselines on synergy, ablation impact, heuristic alignment and predictivity. They call the coalitions functionally indispensable, interpretable computational units. Across layers, coalitions mostly vanish or split, merges are near zero, and persistence is low. They read this as deeper MLPs acting as feature filters and refiners rather than creators.
record.recipe_differences: Uses game-theoretic coalition discovery and neuron ablations in LoRA-fine-tuned LLM MLPs, rather than toy networks trained to represent sparse overcomplete feature sets; it does not measure feature-direction geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Results are reported across three backbones and three scalar IR tasks; the paper reports different OOD drops by task and compares OCA with PAS valuations.

fits_no_version.finding: In LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B and Pythia-6.9B rerankers, the method finds groups of MLP neurons with synergistic ablation effects. Ablating one coalition drops OOD performance by 0.10–0.17. Coalition mean activations reach R2 0.55–0.67 with IR heuristics, far above clustering baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-specific computations in fine-tuned LLM MLPs are carried by synergistic multi-neuron groups rather than single neurons. A single-neuron baseline would be needed to make this a test of distributed representation.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to LoRA-fine-tuned rerankers on scalar IR tasks and is indirect for feature distribution. The paper does not establish that discovered coalitions correspond to the sparse features in the claim. Some reported results are only given as aggregate prose ranges, and portions of the tables have disrupted column layout. The paper notes that its layer-local analysis may underestimate long-range interactions and that its current formulation yields disjoint coalitions.
record.rows_left_out: No per-model, per-task coalition-dynamics rows from Table 3 were included because those rows describe transitions between coalitions, not feature distribution or superposition geometry. Individual Table 1 and Table 6 cells were not extracted where the flattened layout did not clearly support assigning values; the prose-level aggregates are recorded instead.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity sweep, and no feature-direction geometry.
No test of capacity competition or of feature importance determining dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
There is no measure of how many neurons a feature spans relative to single neurons, and no SAE recovery. The coalitions are disjoint partitions produced by the method itself.
No comparison of 1-D directions with multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Every quantitative result compares the authors' method with baselines, so the rows should not link to V4. Inconsistencies a reader may want to check: Section 3 defines ablation as resetting to pre-LoRA weights, while Appendix G zeroes activations. Training is described as 3 epochs in Section 4 but 0.3 and 1 epoch in Appendix F. Table 4 gives an identical base NDCG of 0.18 for all three models. The paper states it fine-tuned on simple features in part to restrict polysemanticity. The coalitions are disjoint by construction, which the authors note despite early-layer polysemy.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test sparse features exceeding network dimensions, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular toy-model geometry.
Does not test whether neurons compete for limited representational capacity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

Provides indirect evidence from coalition analysis in LoRA-fine-tuned scalar-task rerankers only. It does not test SAE recovery or establish feature distribution across general-purpose, unmodified LLM representations.
Does not evaluate SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonicality.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, and Pythia-6.9B (aggregate)

conditions.value: three LLMs; aggregate description, not broken down by model
each layer; exact layers for this distribution not stated

rows.measure: Coalition size distribution and number of neurons covered
rows.value: Heavy-tailed, Zipf-like distribution; each layer has one macro coalition (> 150 neurons), ∼ 100 coalitions of size 2, and approximately 500 clusters with |C| > 1 covering ∼ 14,000 neurons
rows.locator: Appendix G, Intrinsic Evaluation Results; Discussion, Coalition size distribution
rows.note: The authors describe coalitions as computational units. The reported distribution is not broken out by model or task and does not establish that these coalitions correspond to superposed features.
rows.check: The coalition-size distribution is the output of the authors' partitioning algorithm, and is reported only as an aggregate across models and layers. It does not measure how many neurons a model feature occupies. It is not evidence of feature distribution or superposition.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, and Pythia-6.9B rerankers on the tested scalar IR tasks
reader_labels.reason: The authors find multi-neuron coalitions with synergy, substantial coalition-ablation effects, heuristic alignment, and predictive utility (r1–r11), providing indirect evidence for task-related computations involving groups of neurons.
